messages:
maya: Heads up — I'm seeing ~400 accounts stuck in "onboarding: waiting" for >30 days. Most have owner_id = NULL or duplicate contact records. Anyone else spotting this?

oliver: yep, I pulled a sample. Duplicate emails + bad company matching. Looks like the ingestion dedupe missed them.

samir: agree. Also a chunk have health_score calculated without recent telemetry which inflates their score.

maya: proposal: temporary playbook that routes affected accounts into a CSOps "manual-review" queue and pings a reminder to any existing owner, otherwise assign to pool. SLA = 3 business days for triage.

leo: sounds reasonable. Can we restrict to high-risk cohorts only? e.g., status IN ("trial","onboarding") AND health_score < 40 so we don't swamp CS.

maya: good call. here's the quick SQL I used to get the baseline sample:
```
SELECT account_id
FROM accounts
WHERE owner_id IS NULL
  AND created_at < '2025-10-01'
  AND status IN ('trial','onboarding')
  AND health_score < 40;
```

oliver: add a dedupe check join on contacts.email to catch duplicates before assigning. Also we should tag the account with `manual_review:reason=missing-owner` so playbooks can filter.

jen: +1. We should also capture a one-question follow-up to the customer when we triage: "What blocked your onboarding?" and surface the verbatim response to the enablement owner. That will help reduce repeat churn and feed feedback into enablement content.

samir: we can wire that response into the quality/regression pipeline — treat the freeform answer as a labeled attribute for later healthscore tuning.

leo: ops question — who will own the automation and the runbook? Concerned about noisy assignments and extra work for CS.

maya: CSOps will own the runbook and the 'manual-review' tag lifecycle (assign -> triage -> escalate). We'll need a small playbook change in playbook-rules to support the new routing rule. @oliver can you estimate dev effort?

oliver: should be small. Update to playbook-rules service + a new routing predicate and action to set `manual_review`. Estimate ~4 hours dev + 2 hours staging test. I can do it this week.

cs-bot: deploy scheduled — playbook-rules v2.14.0 will roll out to staging at 2025-11-03T02:00Z.

samir: suggest a 1-week dry-run limited to 100 accounts. Metrics to monitor: response rate to the follow-up, triage completion rate within SLA, reassign rate, and delta in renewal-risk signal.

maya: I'll draft the runbook and the monitoring dashboard. Action items: jen owns enablement follow-ups, samir owns metrics, oliver implements the playbook change, and I (maya) will coordinate the dry-run. I'll drop the runbook in #cs-ops-runbook.

jen: ack — will prepare the follow-up template and suggested enablement content.

oliver: I'll post a PR for playbook-rules and link it here when ready, will also notify #eng-ops for review.

maya: thanks all. If no objections we'll start the dry-run on Monday 2025-11-10 (100 accounts).

leo: no objections from me.

maya: great — marking this thread for runbook follow-up and closing the loop after week 1 metrics. :thumbsup:
